task.description: Observed 2026-11-06 across GB-204 steps 1-3: the allowlist is hand-edited TOML every time an edge changes, so I edited it with python three times. Two gaps follow. (1) PRUNE/ADOPT: after a repoint the entry's 'to' crate changes name (miter-inventory -> gaugeblock-inventory) and after a mitigation the edge disappears; a --prune that deletes entries matching no current edge, and an --adopt --ticket KEY that adds entries for unallowlisted edges, would make burn-down mechanical instead of error-prone. (2) GATE HOLE: --check fails for unallowlisted lateral and for upward edges, but passes when the allowlist holds an entry for an edge that no longer exists. That is a silent suppression waiting to be re-armed: if the edge returns, it is excused without anyone deciding. --check should report stale entries and fail on them.
task.title: miter deps --layers should prune and adopt allowlist entries, and fail on an entry that matches no edge

acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06, commit eccb774 (miter).

The gate could see an unallowlisted edge but not an entry that explained nothing. That gap had a body count: a burned edge left its allowlisted exception behind twice today (chalkline-core -> storypole-core, then both outfeed edges), and both times I noticed by eye and deleted it by hand. An entry is now an input to the verdict rather than bookkeeping the verdict ignores.

What changed:
- LayerReport.stale lists entries no lateral edge claimed. It is built from the input allowlist rather than by set difference over edge names, so an entry naming a crate that no longer exists still counts as stale instead of vanishing.
- is_clean() requires stale to be empty, so --check fails with its own message: 'N unallowlisted lateral edge(s), M upward edge(s), K stale allowlist entr(ies)'. The three failure kinds are named separately because they need different fixes.
- --prune deletes stale entries; --adopt --ticket KEY writes an entry for every unallowlisted lateral edge. --adopt without a ticket refuses with 'an exception without an owner is a suppression'.
- Both edit the file textually rather than round-tripping TOML. The allowlist opens with a comment explaining what an entry means and how one leaves the file; a round-trip would delete the prose, and an entry without its explanation is exactly the suppression the file exists to prevent.
- Edits apply before the report is rendered, and the allowlist is re-read afterwards. Without that, --prune --check printed 'violated' for a file it had just cleaned - a verdict that disagrees with the file teaches a reader to distrust verdicts.

Proven on the live workspace rather than asserted: seeded a ghost entry, --check failed naming it, --prune --check exited 0 with 'Verdict: clean' and the entry gone with the header comment intact, and --adopt without --ticket refused.

Found on the way: the layer table never printed the orchestrator layer, though the report has carried it since GB-204, so 'miter deps --layers prints every crate's layer' was false for three crates. Fixed.

And the audit caught this change itself: layers.rs went to 258 and args.rs to 253, both split rather than left over - layers/report.rs and args_deps.rs. The gate wired in the previous commit is already earning its place.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, 277 tests green, audit clean, docs 9 present 0 drifted, layers clean at 0 lateral edges.
